race_context: Whitley County Consolidated Schools (WCCS) is based in Columbia City and runs schools including Columbia City High School, Indian Springs Middle School and Mary Raber Montessori {pm_back_to_school}{pm_brief_0319}. State enrollment counts were 3,690 students in 2023-24, 3,686 in 2024-25 and 3,620 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. Dr. Trent Lehman, formerly superintendent of Southern Wells Community Schools, was hired in December 2025 to become superintendent on July 1, 2026, succeeding the retiring Dr. Laura McDermott {pm_lehman}{wzbd_lehman}.

The board has nine members, each tied to a residence district: three from Columbia City and one each from Columbia, Etna Troy, Jefferson, Thorncreek, Union and Washington townships {wc_roster_2025}{wc_sb_schedule}. Candidates must live in their district, but every voter in the corporation votes in each race; candidates qualify by filing a petition with 10 signatures {wc_sb_schedule}. Dave Smith is board president {pm_lehman}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the county lists four seats — two Columbia City seats and one each for Columbia Township and Thorncreek Township {wc_offices_2026}{wc_cands_2026}. The state list shows 'vote for 1' for the Columbia City race, but the county lists it as 'Columbia City (2)' and its district schedule shows two Columbia City seats elected in 2026, so voters will pick two of the four Columbia City candidates {in_list}{wc_cands_2026}{wc_sb_schedule}.

Who holds the seats now: the Columbia City seats ending in 2026 are held by Katherine (Kate) Method, who is running again, and Heather Shively, who is not on the ballot; the Columbia Township seat is held by David E. Smith and the Thorncreek Township seat by Mary Ann Schaefer, neither of whom is on the ballot {wc_roster_2025}{wc_cands_2026}. At least three new members will join the board.

Party labels: 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party. The county and state lists show Bryan Smethers as Independent, Marc D. Daniel as Democratic, and the other five candidates as Republican {wc_cands_2026}{in_list}.

Superintendent change (Aug. 2025–July 2026): McDermott announced in August 2025 that she would retire June 30, 2026; the board hired the University Search Team and surveyed the public before approving Lehman on Dec. 22, 2025 {pm_search}{pm_lehman}.
Test scores: on spring 2025 ILEARN, 40.2% of WCCS students were proficient in English and 37.5% in math, compared with 40.6% and 42.1% statewide {pm_ilearn}.

Programs and facilities (2026): board agendas included an update on the Radio Road career and technical education (CTE) building and a presentation on Mary Raber Montessori, which had a waiting list for 2026-27 (March 2026) {pm_brief_0319}. In April 2026 the board set caps on out-of-district enrollment for 2026-27 and took up a cell phone policy {pm_briefs_0416}{pm_briefs_0430}.

Budget and operations (2026): agendas included a bus purchase (February), higher school lunch prices for 2026-27 (June), and naming a school representative to the Peabody Public Library board (February and August) {pm_briefs_0221}{pm_brief_0611}{pm_briefs_0812}. The 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 changes how property taxes are collected and distributed, but this guide found no report on its effect on the WCCS budget or any WCCS referendum plan {pm_top2025}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for these races. The only campaign statements found were two letters to the editor from Chris Miller {kpc_miller_0805}{kpc_miller_0910}.

background: Describes himself as the son and husband of teachers and the parent of a young student {kpc_miller_0805}.

items: Says he has spent the past year meeting with teachers, principals, parents, retired educators, community leaders and current and former board members, and that he tried "to listen before forming opinions" {kpc_miller_0910}.

Describes the district's students as the community's future workers and leaders and calls public education an investment in "the future of our community" {kpc_miller_0805}.
